# `default-changed`

default changed

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | `wire` |
| **Default severity** | `warn` in requests, `warn` in responses |
| **Rule IDs** | `default-changed` (both directions), `default-changed-in-request`, `default-changed-in-response` |
| **Status** | Implemented (M5) |
| **Group** | Schemas ([RULES.md section 7](../../RULES.md)) |

## What it detects

A `default` value changed.

## Why this default

When a client omits the field, the server now behaves differently. The JSON is still valid, so it is a warning.

## Example

From test case [`default-changed`](../../test/cases/default-changed/): A default changed: behaviour changes when clients omit the field.

`openapi.yaml`, base → revision:

```diff
  …
          name:
            type: string
-           default: a
+           default: b
```

Findings:

- `default-changed-in-request` · warn · #/components/schemas/Pet

## Policy options

Every rule takes `severity` (`error`, `warn`, `info` or `off`), `fix` and `explanation` in the policy file, for the generic ID or any variant ID above (the more specific ID wins). The policy file arrives in M6; see [POLICY.md](../../POLICY.md).

```yaml
rules:
  default-changed: warn
```

## How to fix

Keep the old default, or announce the change.
